settings.cursorBlinkDesc: Blink the cursor in terminal panes.
settings.dimInactiveDesc: Fade panes you are not working in while a workspace is split.
settings.discreteGpuDesc: Run {product} on the discrete GPU that switcheroo-control lists. Programs in terminals keep the default GPU. On a laptop where another GPU drives the screen, every frame is copied between the two GPUs, which adds latency to terminal text and scrolling. settings.focusOnHoverDesc: Focus a pane after the pointer rests on it. Never interrupts typing in a field.
settings.followSystemDesc: Switch between a light and a dark theme with your system.
settings.fontMissing: Not installed; a fallback font is used
settings.gpuAccelerationDesc: Draw terminals with WebGL so block and box-drawing characters fill their cells. Applies to new terminals.

settings.hibernateIdleDesc: Time without output or input before a hidden agent may hibernate.
settings.hibernateMaxLiveDesc: Hibernation starts once more agent terminals than this are running.
settings.hibernateNote: Hibernating ends everything the agent’s shell runs, including background jobs. Resume starts the agent again from its own saved session.
settings.hideTabCloseDesc: Remove the close button from pane tabs. Close from the palette or a chord.

settings.inputEscapeDesc: What a second Esc does while the prompt holds a draft.
settings.inputModeDesc: Input editor replaces the shell’s input line with a multi-line editor while the shell waits at a prompt. Running programs still get your keys.
settings.keepShells: Keep shells running across a restart

settings.remoteMethodDesc: How the phone reaches this computer. Change it while remote access is off.
settings.remotePairCheck: Approve only if the phone shows {code}.
settings.remotePairDesc: Scan the QR code with {product}’s companion app, or pick this computer in the app and type the code. You approve the phone here.
settings.remotePairReplaces: Says it is the same phone as {name} (last seen {when}). Approving replaces it and closes its connection.
settings.remotePhoneAddressDesc: Optional. The address the phone uses if it is not the listen address, such as a port forward. It must pass TCP through unchanged: the phone pins this computer’s certificate.
settings.remotePhoneAddressInvalid: Enter a host name or IPv4 address and a port, like host.example:8722.
settings.remotePushDescOff: Wake this phone through your server when an agent needs you and the app is not connected. A wake-up carries no text; the phone reads the details from this computer once it connects.
settings.remotePushDescRegistered: On. Your server wakes this phone when an agent needs you and the app is not connected.
settings.remotePushDescWaiting: Waiting for the phone to register. Open the app on the phone and connect.
settings.remotePushNeedsNotify: This phone is not allowed notifications.
settings.remotePushNotSignedIn: Push needs this computer to be signed in to your server.
settings.remotePushServerOff: Your server does not offer push.
settings.remotePushUnreachable: Your server cannot be reached to check push.
settings.remoteRelayDesc: {server} only forwards bytes. The gateway ends TLS with its pinned certificate, so the server cannot read or change the traffic.
settings.remoteRelayError: The relay is not connected ({code}). It retries on its own.
settings.remoteTailnetHelperStopped: The Tailscale helper stopped. Turn remote access off and on to start it again.
settings.remoteTailnetLoginRefused: {product} refused a login link that is not from Tailscale.
settings.remoteTailnetNoIpv4: Tailscale has no IPv4 address for this computer yet, so there is nothing to pair with.
settings.remoteTailnetStateDirUnsafe: {product}’s Tailscale folder is not safe to use: it is a symlink or not owned by you.
settings.remoteTailnetUnavailable: The Tailscale helper could not start.
settings.remoteTailscaleDesc: Install Tailscale on the phone and sign in to the same tailnet. There is no hosted relay and no {product} account.
settings.remoteUnpairBody: {name} is disconnected at once and has to pair again to reach this computer.
settings.restoreWorkspaceDesc: Reopen your workspaces, panes and terminal scrollback the next time {product} starts. Shells are always respawned fresh.
settings.scrollSpeedDesc: Wheel scroll multiplier for terminals, 0.5 to 5.
settings.scrollbackHistoryDesc: Output older than the lines in memory is kept on this machine, encrypted, until the pane closes or the app quits. A clear empties it.
settings.scrollbackLinesDesc: Lines each terminal keeps in memory, 1,000 to 100,000. Older output moves to history on disk. Applies to open terminals.
settings.shellDesc: Program new terminals run, with its arguments, like /usr/bin/fish. Empty uses your login shell. Blocks and the input editor need zsh or bash.
settings.sidebarItemsDesc: Show the git branch and the details extensions add.
settings.sidebarMessageDesc: Show the latest notification or running command.
settings.sidebarPathDesc: Show the workspace folder under its name.
settings.sidebarSshDesc: Show the host a running ssh in the workspace is connected to.
settings.title: Settings
settings.trustWorkspaceFoldersDesc: When {product} resumes or starts Claude in a workspace folder, mark that folder trusted in Claude’s own config (~/.claude.json) so Claude doesn’t ask. This trusts the folder for Claude outside {product} too. Scratch workspaces count too. Never your home folder or sandboxed workspaces. Turning this off doesn’t remove trust already given.
settings.uiFontDesc: Size and weight set the body text; labels and headings scale from them.
settings.warnRiskyPasteDesc: Ask before pasting two or more lines into a terminal: a shell may run each line as soon as it arrives. A single line is always pasted without its trailing newline or control characters. Agents can’t change this.
settings.wheelSmoothScrollDesc: Animate scrollback when you scroll with a mouse wheel. Trackpads already scroll smoothly, and reduced motion turns this off.
settings.wheelZoomDesc: Scrolling over a terminal or the editor with the key held changes its font size. Keyboard zoom keeps working either way.

folderAccessBlocked.body: Shells in {product} may keep failing to read these folders. Quit {product}, choose “Quit and end shells” if it asks, and open it again to restore access.
folderAccessBlocked.title: macOS is blocking {folders}

workspace folder, are discarded when this shell exits. Add a writable folder
in Settings › Sandbox to keep them.
paneBanner.integrationNotLoaded: Shell integration not loaded ({reason}): this shell runs without prompt marks, the CLI or agent hooks. Open a new pane to try again.
paneBanner.keepShellsLost: This shell will not survive a restart.
paneBanner.noShell: No shell was started. This workspace only runs sandboxed.
paneBanner.otherWorkspace: the pane belongs to another workspace
paneBanner.sandboxEnded: its sandbox ended while {product} was closed
paneBanner.sandboxNotKept: this workspace's sandbox was started without tmux
paneBanner.tmuxMissing: tmux {version} or newer is not installed

quit.keptBody: Quit and keep shells leaves them running in tmux, and the next start reattaches them. Quit and end shells ends them.
quit.message: Quitting ends or discards everything listed here.
quit.title: Quit and lose this work?
quit.unanswered: The window did not answer, so it may have running commands or unsaved files

sandboxSoftware.body: Install {packages} to start this sandboxed workspace’s terminals.
sandboxSoftware.title: Sandbox needs software

signIn.failed: Sign-in did not finish. Return to {product} and try again.
